record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests shared representations across seeds, architectures, and objectives using cross-validated prediction of individual dimensions, rather than a model-scale sweep or direct distance comparison.
record.gate_note: The study tests dimension-level predictability and brain similarity in vision models. It does not sweep model size or capability, compare vision with language models, or test whether representations become more aligned as models scale. The study describes several figure results qualitatively without reporting exact plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well each principal component of one vision network is linearly predicted by other networks. It does this across 20 seeds of one architecture, 19 architectures, 9 objectives and 4 training-image sets, with an untrained control and alternative mappings. This is a different method aimed at the shared-representation question behind V3, V4, V6 and V7. There is no scale sweep and no language model.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that diverse vision networks, across seeds, architectures, objectives and (preliminarily) visual diets, converge on a small core of universal dimensions amid many idiosyncratic ones. These universal dimensions are the most brain-aligned and drive conventional network–brain RSA. The authors attribute shared untrained dimensions to image statistics. They leave open whether convergence reflects efficient coding or a shared model of the world's generative factors.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cross-validated prediction of principal-component dimensions from other networks and fMRI responses, plus RSA after reducing networks to universal dimensions. It does not measure convergence through a size or capability sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: One-to-one mapping produces lower universality and brain-similarity values than ridge regression, although the trends remain strongly correlated; ordinary least squares gives highly consistent variation.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-100 universal penultimate-layer PCs organise images semantically (RSA with caption embeddings r=0.35). The least-universal PCs (r=0.00) and untrained universal PCs (r=0.03) do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dimensions shared across trained vision models encode high-level semantic content, whereas model-specific or untrained shared dimensions do not.

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing networks to their top 10 or top 5 universal dimensions leaves network-to-visual-cortex RSA unchanged or slightly higher in all trained sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment between models and the brain is carried by the dimensions shared across models.

record.problems: The main comparisons share visual training data for the architecture- and task-varied sets; the varied-visual-diet analysis is preliminary and includes four models. The paper reports many relevant results in plots without exact values in the text. It uses one natural-image fMRI dataset and does not test scale, capability, or cross-modal convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Individual-network, individual-subject, and ROI follow-up plots are not given separate rows because the text reports their trends as consistent with the aggregate findings and does not state separate values. See Figures S1–S3, S9–S10.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or capability. Cross-architecture and cross-objective sharing is shown, but not whether it grows with scale.
No vision–language comparison. Caption embeddings are used only to interpret the universal dimensions.
No unit- or basis-level matching. Only vision CNNs (ResNet-18) are tested across seeds.
No whole-representation or variance-weighted mapping loss, no stitching, no relative representations, no unpaired mapping.
No neuron, circuit or SAE-feature matching; the dimensions are principal components.
Only the mapping method is varied (ridge, OLS, one-to-one). There is no variation of input set, out-of-distribution inputs, neighbour count or kernel measures; all analyses use 872 NSD/COCO images.
No plateau test. Shared objective is not separated from shared data in the visual-diet set, and the common-reality account is not tested.

missing.what: Universality is shown by PC-rank decade. Low-rank PCs are usually universal, but top-10 PCs can score as low as third-decade PCs. This matters for judging whether the shared subspace is the high-variance one, which affects V4 mapping loss and V3.
Per-network universality trend (every network contains universal dimensions; the effect is not confined to a few models), relevant to cross-architecture convergence.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Universality is the median linear-prediction correlation per PC over 872 images, with no variance weighting. So 'most dimensions idiosyncratic' may largely reflect low-variance PCs, which is why the V4 label is limits_scope rather than challenges. Architecture and objective sets share ImageNet data; the authors acknowledge this. No exact proportions are given; most results are density plots.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep and no test of whether alignment rises with size or performance.
No paired image-caption alignment test or comparison of vision and language models.
Tests shared dimensions, not whether individual units or bases match; does not test other modalities.
Tests prediction of individual dimensions across models, not complete representation interchangeability, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired inputs.
Does not identify recurring neurons, circuits, or SAE features across models; its dimensions are principal components.
Compares regression and one-to-one mapping procedures, but not different input datasets, out-of-distribution inputs, neighbour counts, or a broad set of similarity measures.
Does not establish a plateau or determine whether convergence reflects a common model of reality; the varied-visual-diet analysis is preliminary.

rows.subject: 20 ResNet-18 models (trained, aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured prediction of each target principal component from other models' activations; related dimension universality to brain similarity.

conditions.value: different random initializations; same architecture, task, and training data

rows.measure: Dimension universality and brain similarity; cross-validated prediction from other models and fMRI responses.
rows.value: Universality scores span 0 to 1; most dimensions are idiosyncratic, while a smaller subset has exceptionally high universality and brain similarity.
rows.note: Aggregate result for the set. The authors also report a consistent trend across each individual network, layer, fMRI subject, and multiple visual-cortex ROIs.
rows.check: Link is correct. Only a small subset of dimensions is highly universal. The paper gives no count or proportion; the evidence is density plots only.

rows.subject: 19 models with varied architectures (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: trained on ImageNet for object classification
rows.operation_detail: Measured prediction of target principal components from other models' activations and from fMRI responses.
rows.value: Most dimensions are idiosyncratic; a subset has exceptionally high universality and brain similarity despite architecture differences.
rows.note: Aggregate result for the varied-architecture set.
rows.check: The set varies architecture, not random initialization, so it does not bear on V3 (seeds). It bears on V4 (linear predictability) and V7 (incomplete sharing).

rows.subject: 9 ResNet-50 models with varied training objectives (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured prediction of target principal components from other models' activations and from fMRI responses.
rows.value: Most dimensions are idiosyncratic; a subset has exceptionally high universality and brain similarity across models with different objectives.
rows.note: Aggregate result for the varied-objective set.
rows.check: The set varies training objective at fixed ResNet-50, not seeds, so V3 does not apply.

rows.subject: 20 untrained ResNet-18 models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured prediction of target principal components across untrained models and from fMRI responses.
rows.baseline: Trained networks with varied initializations, architectures, or objectives.
rows.value: Untrained models also have shared dimensions, but these have substantially lower brain similarity; the universality–brain-similarity relationship is shallow and approximately linear rather than sharply increasing at high universality.
rows.note: Shows that shared dimensions can occur without training, while their brain similarity differs from the trained-model pattern.
rows.check: Control row. Untrained seed-varied ResNet-18s also have dimensions shared across all networks, which the authors attribute to image statistics. So some seed-level sharing does not require learning. The state reflects that shared dimensions exist, not a learned effect.

rows.subject: Trained model sets: varied initializations, architectures, and objectives (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared dimension universality and brain similarity across sampled network layers.
rows.measure: Universality and brain similarity by layer.
rows.value: No strong layer effect; highly universal dimensions occur even in the deepest sampled layers.
rows.note: The authors report the trend across all sampled layers.
rows.check: This is an aggregate across three trained sets. Only the seed-varied panel bears on V3; the other panels bear on V4.

rows.subject: 20 ResNet-18 models trained on Tiny ImageNet (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed universality and brain similarity using ordinary least squares instead of ridge regression.
rows.measure: Relationship between dimension universality and brain similarity.
rows.value: The authors report that the variation in the metrics is highly consistent with the ridge-regression results.
rows.note: Alternative mapping procedure; the paper gives no exact plotted values in the text.
rows.check: For V6 the state should be absent. Per-dimension scores under OLS are 'highly consistent' with ridge, so the measure does not depend on the regression choice. Observed applies only to V3/V4.

rows.subject: 20 ResNet-18 models trained on Tiny ImageNet (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed universality and brain similarity using one-to-one feature mapping without regression reweighting.
rows.measure: Relationship between dimension universality and brain similarity.
rows.value: All values are lower, but the results remain strongly correlated with those from ridge regression and show similar trends.
rows.note: Mapping choice changes score magnitude but not the reported overall trend.
rows.check: For V6 this is partial dependence. One-to-one mapping lowers all values, but they remain strongly correlated with ridge and show the same trends.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 varied-task set, penultimate-layer top 100 universal dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared UMAP embeddings of image representations with caption-based semantic embeddings using RSA.
rows.measure: RSA correlation between UMAP and semantic embeddings.
rows.note: The authors describe the universal dimensions as grouping semantically related images.
rows.check: This RSA of universal dimensions against caption embeddings characterises what the shared dimensions encode. It does not measure cross-model convergence, and the subject set varies task, not seeds. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 varied-task set, penultimate-layer 100 least universal dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared UMAP embeddings of image representations with caption-based semantic embeddings using RSA.
rows.measure: RSA correlation between UMAP and semantic embeddings.
rows.note: The authors also report no clear semantic organization in the visualization.
rows.check: This is a comparator for R8: the least-universal dimensions give r=0.00. It is not a convergence measure.

rows.subject: Untrained ResNet-18 set, penultimate-layer top 100 universal dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared UMAP embeddings of image representations with caption-based semantic embeddings using RSA.
rows.measure: RSA correlation between UMAP and semantic embeddings.
rows.note: The untrained universal dimensions emphasize low-level image properties rather than the reported semantic organization.
rows.check: Untrained universal dimensions give r=0.03 against semantics. This is not a convergence measure.

rows.subject: Trained model sets with varied initializations, architectures, and objectives (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed network-to-visual-cortex RSA after retaining only the top ten universal dimensions.
rows.measure: RSA between network and visual-cortex representational dissimilarity matrices.
rows.value: Little or no decrease; the authors report a slight improvement for all three trained model sets.
rows.note: Aggregate comparison across the three trained model sets.
rows.check: This is network-to-brain RSA after reducing each network to its top 10 universal dimensions. It measures brain alignment, not model-to-model convergence.

rows.subject: Trained model sets with varied initializations, architectures, and objectives (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed network-to-visual-cortex RSA after retaining only the top five universal dimensions.
rows.measure: RSA between network and visual-cortex representational dissimilarity matrices.
rows.value: Little or no decrease; the authors report a slight improvement for all three trained model sets.
rows.note: Aggregate comparison across the three trained model sets.
rows.check: Same as R11, with the top 5 dimensions. It measures brain alignment, not convergence between models.

rows.subject: 4 IPCL AlexNet-GN models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured universality and brain similarity across models trained with different visual diets.
rows.value: Most dimensions are idiosyncratic, but a subset has exceptionally high universality and brain similarity across the varied visual diets.
rows.locator: Discussion; Section 4.2.1; Figure S12; Table S3
rows.note: The authors characterize this as a preliminary analysis.
rows.check: The four models share architecture and objective and differ in training data, so the row is not a seeds test for V3. It bears on V7's shared-data explanation and on V4. The authors call the analysis preliminary.
